transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CSM), Jamie Park (VantageThera Head of ML), Ravi Patel (Eng Manager), Lena Ortiz (Security Lead), Tommy Nguyen (Product)

Summary: quick QBR/health check, looks like usage ramped in June mostly read ops and some hallucination of cost due to long generation, customer interested in private deployment feasibility, want numbers for dedicated commit.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Alex Kim: Hey team, thanks for carving out time today for the QBR, we wanted to walk through usage, cost, reliability incidents in June and a roadmap discussion for the fall. Quick intros?
00:12 Jamie Park: Yeah hi Jamie here, Head of ML at VantageThera. On the call to figure out reliability and cost. Sorry been heads down with the new triage flow.
00:18 Ravi Patel: Ravi, eng lead. We own the inference infra and the orchestration around calls into Redwood.
00:23 Lena Ortiz: Lena, security. I'm here for private deployment questions and K-M-S encryption stuff.
00:27 Tommy Nguyen: Tommy, PM. Looking to understand latency impact on product and roadmap constraints.
00:33 Alex Kim: Great. Priya, quick context on usage trends?
00:36 Priya Desai: Yeah so from Redwood side we saw a 3.6x increase in token volume in June, most of that coming from longer generation due to the new summary feature -- peak hour was about 2:30pm PST for you folks. We noticed an increase in p95 latency during the regional failover on 6/18 where some requests routed to a lower-capacity pool.
00:56 Jamie Park: That failover cost us, yeah we had 12 minutes total of elevated latencies and a small error spike which our SLO flagged. Can you remind me why it fell back to the small pool, I thought we were on reserved capacity?
01:08 Priya Desai: You are on a reserved pool but there was an autoscaler glitch where burst settings didn't kick for the reservation because of an internal node drain. The smart-routing fallback picked a cheaper compatible model which increased latency. We logged it as an incident — root cause tied to autoscale configuration + node eviction timing.
01:28 Marcus Lee: We're classifying this as severity 3 from our side, and we have a plan to add a hard capacity buffer for your account to prevent future spillovers.
01:36 Ravi Patel: Ok cool, that's helpful. On the cost side we got a surprise spike - our finance team flagged a 42% month-over-month increase in hosted spend. Any immediate levers to recommend?
01:48 Priya Desai: A few quick levers: enable prefix/KV cache (I know your team uses lots of repeated prompts, the cache would cut token generation), switch to a quantized model variant for background workloads, and adjust batching settings in the SDK. Also, dedicated capacity can reduce per-token costs if you have steady throughput.
02:07 Jamie Park: When you say KV cache, do you mean the K-V cash? The transcription sometimes, sorry -- but yes we do repeat patterns across users. What's a realistic hit rate?
02:16 Priya Desai: Our typical hit rate for that workload shape is 18-35% depending on prompt homogenity; for VantageThera with many templated queries you might hit 30%+ which is substantial.
02:26 Tommy Nguyen: Curious about latency tradeoffs. If we enable larger batching to save cost, what's the impact on p50 and p95?
02:32 Priya Desai: Batching helps throughput cost but increases tail latency. You can set max latency SLO and Redwood will cap batch waiting time. We also support continuous batching where small windows collect quickly so p50 isn't impacted much, p95 could move by ~40-80ms depending on model and sequence length. We'll run a microbench with your mix.
02:52 Jamie Park: Cool. On private deployment - Lena has a long list of compliance reqs including KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 attestations. Lena, any specifics?
03:02 Lena Ortiz: Yes we need BYOK via customer K-M-S/H-S-M, retention controls for logs, and an air-gap option for limited sets. Also multi-tenant isolation on the control plane is a concern.
03:15 Alex Kim: Redwood Private supports customer KMS integrations and provides audit logs, plus an option for on-prem package. For air-gapped it's a higher-touch ops engagement. Priya, can you run through what we usually offer?
03:27 Priya Desai: Sure - we have a private control plane option where the customer manages the VPC, we support customer-managed KMS, we can enable enhanced audit log retention. The on-prem package includes an ops bundle for installs. For your needs we'd recommend the private deployment with managed control-plane in your VPC or a full on-prem if required by legal.
03:47 Ravi Patel: How different is the infra footprint between dedicated and private? We're worried about ops cost.
03:53 Priya Desai: Dedicated is still Redwood-hosted hardware but reserved for you, so ops overhead is minimal. Private means you host or we install in your environment, so there's more customer-side ops and some professional services cost. Dedicated hits a nice sweet spot if you want predictable throughput and lower ops.
04:14 Jamie Park: On accuracy/regressions - we introduced a prompt tweak in June that lowered latency but slightly changed tokenization and we saw a bump in bad outputs. Is there an eval pipeline we can hook into Redwood to detect regressions before rollout?
04:28 Marcus Lee: Yes we have Redwood Optimize integrations: you can upload prompt sets and we'll run regression alerts tied to quality metrics, plus model variant comparisons.
04:36 Tommy Nguyen: Great, we'd like to run that.
04:40 Jamie Park: On the numbers, can you show committed pricing vs pay-as-you-go for our March-June baseline?
04:47 Alex Kim: We'll send a committed-savings spreadsheet. For ballpark: dedicated reserved pools typically reduce per-token cost 20-40% depending on utilization. Private has a different pricing model with platform fees. We'll put apples-to-apples scenarios in the doc.
04:59 Lena Ortiz: Also need to validate encryption in transit and at rest and if audit logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
05:06 Priya Desai: Yes, TLS for transit, encryption at rest, and logs can be forwarded to Splunk/Datadog or your SIEM with structured events. We'll include a security pack with endpoints and sample configurations.
05:18 Jamie Park: There was a question from finance: if we commit to dedicated, what's the penalty for underutilization?
05:24 Alex Kim: We have flexible burst and autoscale policies. Commitments are priced by monthly commitments and we can include a right-sizing clause in the contract; Marcus can model a ramp schedule that protects against heavy penalties.
05:36 Ravi Patel: For the benchmark, what hardware will you run? We prefer to see both an a100-style baseline and a quantized-cpu sim if available.
05:44 Priya Desai: We'll run on our dedicated c7g-80 equivalent and also show a quantized run on a condensed path to show cost delta. Note that quantization results vary by model family. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
05:58 Jamie Park: What about multi-region failover - can Redwood guarantee failover within our SLO? Our app needs less than 300ms p95 during regional issues.
06:06 Priya Desai: We can't legally promise across all edges in a basic hosted plan but with Dedicated + multi-region routing and committed capacity we can architect to meet that SLO; private on-prem reduces cross-region concerns but increases ops. We'll propose an architecture diagram.
06:20 Tommy Nguyen: Anything on billing granularity? Daily vs monthly? We need daily token breakdowns for show-back to product teams.
06:27 Alex Kim: We provide token-level billing with per-route breakdowns and you can pull via API or get daily CSV reports.
06:33 Jamie Park: Okay. Let's talk incident in June — any mitigation to avoid the autoscaler eviction race?
06:38 Priya Desai: We recommend two changes: add a hard buffer to your reserved pool and tune the cluster drain hooks so evictions wait for active pipeline drains. We'll supply a runbook.
06:49 Ravi Patel: That runbook will be great. Also on retention - we need control to set logs retention to 90 days for debug and 7 years for audit-only logs.
06:59 Lena Ortiz: Right, and ensuring PII is never stored in logs - can Redwood redact by default?
07:05 Marcus Lee: We offer configurable log redaction rules and can support an additional filter that scrubs PII. We'll include options and sample config.
07:18 Jamie Park: Good. So immediate actions are pricing scenarios, a benchmark, and the private-deploy feasibility. Anything else?
07:23 Alex Kim: We'll also include an incident remediation plan and the rightsize recommendations for July-August.
07:29 Tommy Nguyen: Can you also add cost projections if we roll out the new summary feature to 60% of users? Finance will need that for budget forecasts.
07:35 Alex Kim: Yes we'll model that.
07:38 Priya Desai: I'll run a micro-bench with your July traces — please share the sample CSV with token distribution and typical sequence lengths.
07:47 Jamie Park: We'll share by EOD tomorrow.
07:50 Alex Kim: Great. Any final questions from Lena on compliance?
07:53 Lena Ortiz: Just to confirm: K-M-S integration + audit log forwarding + retention are all supported for private?
07:58 Alex Kim: Yes, supported. We'll document the exact steps and options in the security pack.
08:03 Marcus Lee: We'll also propose a staged rollout plan: start with dedicated reserved pool for 30 days, run benchmarks, then pilot private if needed.
08:12 Jamie Park: Sounds reasonable.
08:15 Alex Kim: Ok we'll wrap with a recap and action items.
08:18 Jamie Park: Thanks everyone.

--- End of transcript ---

Recap:
- Root cause of June incident: autoscaler/node-eviction race leading to fallback to lower-capacity pool. Action: add hard buffer and tune drain hooks.
- Cost: June spike due to longer generation; levers are KV cache, batching, quantized model variants, or move to dedicated.
- Security: Private supports BYOK KMS, audit logs forwarding, log redaction; Redwood to provide security pack and sample configs.
- Next steps: pricing scenarios, production trace upload, benchmarks, private feasibility call.

References mentioned: pricing spreadsheet (link to be shared), security pack (link to be shared), benchmark artifact (to be provided by Redwood).
